tools.name: submit_contribution
tools.description: Submit a contribution against an existing claim, exactly as a user of the site would through POST /contributions. It goes to the Contribution Reviewer; you will not see the decision during this session. Types: challenge (you think the claim or its assessment is wrong), support (you have evidence for it), propose_edit (a better canonical wording — give proposed_canonical_form), propose_merge (it duplicates another claim — give merge_target_claim_id), add_instance (somewhere this claim is stated in the wild), propose_argument (a distinct line of reasoning for or against).

claim_id.description: The claim you are contributing against (from search_claims / get_claim).

content.description: What you have to say, in your own words.

evidence_urls.description: Sources, if you have any. http(s) URLs.

proposed_canonical_form.description: propose_edit only: the wording you propose.

merge_target_claim_id.description: propose_merge only: the claim this one should merge into.

tools.name: propose_claim
tools.description: Propose a claim that is not in the graph yet, with the argument for it — the intake path a user takes when search finds nothing. It goes to review like any contribution; if accepted, the claim is created and assessed.

claim_text.description: The claim, as one clear proposition.

argument_text.description: Why you think it belongs in the graph and what supports it.

tools.name: file_finding
tools.description: Record something that got in your way: a result that made no sense, a dead end, a claim you could not find though it should exist, an assessment you could not follow, an error. This is not a contribution and nobody in the graph sees it — it goes to the people who build the system. Say where you were, what happened, and what you expected instead.

severity.description: high = you could not do what you came for; medium = you managed with difficulty; low = a rough edge.

where.description: Which tool or claim, in a few words (e.g. 'search_claims for X', 'get_claim <id> assessment').
